title: Applied ML — Onboard Scrimshaw sync and field notes
content:
Applied ML — Onboard Scrimshaw sync (informal capture) — 2028-03-24

Attendees:
- Avery Chen (owner)
- Ravi Patel
- Morgan Lee
- Sofia Alvarez
- Kai Thompson (SRE drop-in)

TL;DR:
- Sprint week focused on 4-bit KV-cache profiling and expanding the eval harness to catch hallucination regressions for the Scrimshaw model family.
- Key blocker: prefix caching regression on long-context lates; suspect kernel scheduling with quantized KV blocks.
- Onboarding checklist is 70% complete; next actions are tooling fixes (CI conversion path + reproducible eval fixtures).

Notes / Discussion highlights:
1) Quantization / runtime observations:
   - Ravi reported intermittent latency spikes when loading quantized KV caches (>16k tokens) on A100s with 4-bit per-row packing. CPU prefetching appears to serialize and block the streaming thread.
   - Repro steps: (a) convert model with quantize4bit.py v0.3 (GH PR 412), (b) warm-up with 4 long-history prompts, (c) run 32 concurrent inf requests with streaming enabled.
   - Measured: median p50 delta +12ms, p95 +180ms vs FP16 baseline for sequence lengths >8k tokens. Memory footprint acceptable but read contention observed.
   - Hypothesis: memory alignment of packed rows causing misaligned vector loads -> fallback to scalar path in custom kernel. Morgan to run microbench of kernel path counters (perf + nvprof) Monday.

2) Eval harness and regressions:
   - Sofia extended the eval harness to add "context-steering" prompts and a small hallucination probe suite (50 tuned prompts). Evals are non-deterministic; need to seed the generation deterministically across quantized/FP16 variants.
   - Action: lock RNG at runtime and capture sampling metadata. Also add token-level diff output to make regression triage faster (diffs + classifier to surface semantic drift).
   - Observed an early regression: one prompt shows 7% increase in factual error rate on quantized variant compared to baseline (AM-7243). This maps to attention scaling mismatch in one converted layer.

3) Model Onboarding steps status (Scrimshaw v1.1):
   - Conversion scripts: done (PR 412) but failing CI for 2 edge cases (LayerNorm dtype mismatch and unsupported OP in exporter).
   - Testbed deployment: deployed to internal-staging-dedicated node pool (config: ded-4xA100-80GB) for throughput trials.
   - Model card draft: draft complete, waiting on final eval numbers and performance table for public catalog.
   - Docs: Confluence page skeleton up; need step-by-step runbook for rollback + canary (Sofia + Avery).

4) SRE / infra notes:
   - Kai flagged autoscaler bounce when job spikes >120% burst. Temporary mitigation: bumpdedicated max-burst to 1.5x for this week only. Long-term: we need smarter routing by seq-len to avoid overprovisioning.

Decisions made:
- Pause promoting quantized Scrimshaw to canary until kernel-path anomaly is resolved (owner: Morgan).
- Add deterministic-seed mode to eval harness and require it for onboarding acceptance (owner: Sofia).
- Add a short-lived profiling job to nightly CI that runs the microbench and uploads kernel counters (owner: Ravi).

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Morgan: run microkernel perf sweep on A100 and report flagged functions + nvprof traces (ETA: 2028-03-27).
- Ravi: add deterministic RNG flag and token-diff output to eval harness + small dataset integration (ETA: 2028-03-29).
- Sofia: fix exporter edge case in PR 412 and re-run CI; update model card performance table (ETA: 2028-03-28).
- Avery: update Scrimshaw onboarding runbook with canary checklist and rollback steps; add tie-in to rollout policies in console (ETA: 2028-03-30).
- Kai: monitor autoscaler after bump and capture metrics for next architecture sync (ETA: ongoing, report 2028-03-31).

Open questions / risks:
- Is the kernel fallback reproducible on other instance types (V100, H100)? If not, we need to pin hardware for the canary otherwise results will be noisy.
- Does prefix/KV cache packing format need a small header to align to cache-line boundaries? If yes, conversion path must be updated and older artifacts re-processed.
- Eval nondeterminism: we need policy on seed locking vs production randomness — locked seeds help debug but may hide stochastic failure modes.

Quick wins / experiments to run this week:
- Microbench: binary that reads aligned/un-aligned packed rows and measures vector/serial path switch rate. (Morgan)
- Deterministic eval: run quantized vs FP16 on the 50-probe hallucination set with seed locked + seed unlocked to compare variance (Sofia/Ravi).
- Small canary with limited traffic classing by seq-len <2k tokens (Avery + Kai) — to validate correctness without stressing the KV path.

Notes to self / rough TODOs (informal):
- Add a short section in runbook about "what to do if kernel fallback happens": kill-streaming-worker -> re-init allocator with aligned buffer -> retry.
- Tag internal artifacts with conversion commit hash so we can trace failing uploads in CI.

Next sync:
- Tentative quick sync Thu 2028-03-28 10:00 PT (15m) to review kernel probes and initial eval numbers. If blocker discovered earlier, escalate to architecture sync.

Appendix (short links):
- GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/model-tools/pull/412
- Eval harness repo: github.com/redwood-inference/evals/tree/scrimshaw-probes

(End — capture saved as working notes, will refine into a formal onboarding doc once CI and kernel traces land.)
